reading.body:
GitHub's only tracked AI product is a free education tier of Copilot, not infrastructure.

The record covers one product, GitHub Copilot for Education, offered free to verified students and educators aged 13 and older under GitHub Education terms. It lists no lawsuits, no MCP servers, and no other filings. That is the whole of what the data supports.

For AI specifically, this is a distribution fact rather than a compute fact. Copilot is a coding assistant, and the tracked decision here is who gets it at no cost, which is students and educators. Nothing in the data describes where that inference runs, how much power it draws, or what buildings house it. The page cannot speak to the grid constraint because it contains no capacity, energy, or site information at all.

The gap is the story. A company described as an AI-powered developer platform used by millions appears here with a single education product and no legal or infrastructure record, so any claim about GitHub's compute footprint would have to come from somewhere other than this data.

profile_text.body:
GitHub describes itself as an AI-powered developer platform, saying it is the world's most widely adopted one, where millions of developers, businesses, and the largest open source community build software. According to its site, it provides AI and automation tools intended to help users build and ship software faster, from a first line of code through to final deployment. The company is listed here as GitHub (Microsoft).

Its tracked AI product is GitHub Copilot for Education, which the company describes as offering code suggestions and chat. It is aimed at verified students and educators aged 13 and older, with student age given as 13 and older for verified students. It is free for verified students and educators 13 and over, and falls under GitHub Education terms.

The available material does not include any litigation, regulatory filings, or other records for the company.
